A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of Anomaly-Preference Image Generation. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-B support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original APO generation, downstream detection and classification results on MVTec AD, together with component and parameter ablations, including Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original APO experiments and appendix ablations and reports revised downstream comparison results in Tables 2 and 3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 4 retain the same APO objective, time-aware LoRA capacity allocation, hierarchical sampling, and deviation-based localization. The changed downstream classifier is an evaluation setting, not a change to APO.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MVTec AD with the same generation, detection, localization, and classification tasks. Table 3 retains the same 14 classification categories; no dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: AnomalyAny is removed from the downstream detection comparison in Table 2 and classification comparison in Table 3, while remaining in the generation comparisons. Other comparator memberships are retained, making this a limited removal.

E3.justification: Table 3 and Section 5.4 change the stated classification backbone from ResNet-18 to ResNet-34. The reference/evaluation split, generated sample counts, metrics, and U-Net evaluation remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects rerunning experiments or correcting the description.

E4.justification: The CPO/TACA component ablations in Table 5, rank sensitivity analysis in Figure 3, and regularization-coefficient ablation in Appendix A and Table 6 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Table 3 substantially replaces the classification results under a different stated backbone: APO's reported average changes from 82.15% to 72.06%, and the leading baseline changes from DualAnoDiff at 79.67% to AnomalyDiffusion at 70.25%. These are not same-setting performance changes. Table 2 also revises SeaS scores, including grid AP-P from 59.1 to 76.3, and both tables remove AnomalyAny results. Tables 1 and 4-6 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The main-text definitions and equations and Appendix B's trajectory-level KL derivation, reward reparameterization, and APO objective derivation are unchanged. No assumptions, proofs, or mathematical corrections are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about annotation-free preference alignment, TACA and hierarchical sampling, and superior synthesis and downstream detection performance.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, fidelity-diversity interpretations, and Appendix A's adaptation/overfitting discussion are retained. No substantive limitations or qualifications are added; the classification interpretation remains unchanged despite the revised rankings.

D1.justification: The documented downstream classifier architecture changes from ResNet-18 to ResNet-34. Section 5.3's diffusion initialization, LoRA ranks, optimizer, sampling settings, hardware, and generated-pair count remain unchanged, with no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to diffusion generation and preference optimization are unchanged. AnomalyAny remains cited and discussed despite its removal from two comparisons.

P1.justification: v3 replaces the erroneous ICML template running header with the paper title, adds Tong Zhang as a corresponding author, and makes limited edits to result summaries. The narrative and section ordering are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 lose the AnomalyAny column groups and are reformatted, with Table 2 enlarged. Figure 3 and nearby material are resized or repositioned, and the conclusion and references reflow. The same figures and remaining tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Header and table cleanup is outweighed by new reporting inconsistencies. In v1, Table 3's APO average of 82.15% matches its 14 category scores to rounding; v3 reports 72.06% although its displayed scores average 77.21%, without explaining another aggregation. The retained claim of a pronounced metal-nut advantage also conflicts with v3's 78.48% for APO versus 82.81% for AnomalyDiffusion. These are limited reporting regressions while the method, theory, and most evidence remain intact.
